html:
Maskat, or Masqat, was a small medieval principality on the western shore of the Caspian Sea, between Shirvan and Derbent, in what is now northern Azerbaijan. It is shown here in 1100. It has nothing to do with Muscat in Oman.

Arab geographers of the 10th century mention it, and its name may echo the ancient Massagetae. It lay on the narrow coastal road that ran north past Derbent to the steppe, between Shirvan, the Lezgian land of Lakz and Derbent. Its own rulers were soon overshadowed by the Shirvanshahs, who absorbed it. Little more is known.
